title: Subdomain Examples Explain How Services Share a Domain

cover.subtitle: Names, DNS, hosting, and HTTPS work together.
cover.visual: One domain branches to four service cards for www, blog, app, and support.

sections.name: 01-hierarchy
sections.heading: Subdomain names show a hierarchy rather than a page path
sections.scene: A DNS name tree highlights blog.example.com while a separate URL path card shows /blog.
sections.alt: A DNS hierarchy distinguishes a subdomain from a page path.

sections.name: 02-services
sections.heading: Useful subdomains separate services with clear responsibilities
sections.scene: Four service cards for website, app, support, and status connect to one domain with owner labels.
sections.alt: Separate services share a domain and keep operational owners.

sections.name: 03-setup
sections.heading: A working subdomain needs DNS and an accepting destination
sections.scene: Three stages show hostname verification, DNS target, and hosting acceptance before an HTTPS test.
sections.alt: A subdomain requires DNS configuration and a receiving service.

sections.name: 04-lifecycle
sections.heading: Certificates and retirement complete the subdomain lifecycle
sections.scene: An inventory card connects certificate checks, monitoring, and a retired-service cleanup step.
sections.alt: A hostname inventory includes certificate checks and retirement.
